title: Prefill-Decode Demultiplexer: Latency Provenance and Stage Smoothing
author: Maya Chen
description: Context: Interactive workloads continue to show bimodal latency tails when we treat prefill and decode as a single undifferentiated pipeline. Motivation: reduce tail latency and KV cache amplification while keeping high throughput for background/throughput traffic. This PR introduces a lightweight prefill-decode demultiplexer that classifies requests at enqueue-time using a low-cost latency provenance signal and routes them into specialized pipeline lanes with stage-smoothing and adaptive thresholds. Summary of changes: - New demux stage (runtime/scheduling/prefill_demux.cc/.h): samples token-level provenance (prefill size, cache hit heuristic, observed kernel queue depth) and assigns one of three lanes: fast-speculative, conservative-prefill, or decode-only. - Lossy prefill aggregation (runtime/prefill/aggregator.*): aggregates small concurrent prefill chunks destined for the same KV shard using a lossy coalescer that keeps representative KV primes to reduce duplicate warms. The coalescer has tunable fidelity and falls back to exact prefill when quality drop is detected. - Stage smoothing controller (runtime/scheduling/stage_smoother.*): per-lane leaky-bucket concurrency limiter that smooths burstiness between prefill and decode handoff, reducing kernel scheduling jitter and tail amplification. - Latency provenance tracing (observability/tracing/prefill_provenance_events.md + tags): new trace tags and sampling logic so we can attribute p95/p99 latency to demux decisions and coalescing. - Rollback and conservative fallback (runtime/scheduling/fallback_policy.*): when the demux lane shows regression in quality (measured via sample evals), traffic is automatically rolled back to the conservative lane. - Tests and benchmarks (tests/prefill_demux_unit.cc, perf/benchmarks/prefill_demux_bench.py): unit tests for demux classifier thresholds and microbenchmarks showing tail improvements. Motivation and behavior notes: - The demux uses a tiny per-request fixed-size probe (4 bytes of provenance) to avoid adding allocs. - Lossy aggregation is conservative: it merges only when KV affinity and token-range overlap exceed a tunable threshold. - Stage smoothing uses a token-bucket that prefers keeping prefill throughput up to configured SLO, then limits burst transfer to decode to avoid sudden kernel queue spikes. Checklist: - [x] Demux classifier implementation and unit tests - [x] Aggregator with fidelity knob and fallback - [x] Stage smoother with configurable SLOs - [x] End-to-end perf harness added - [x] Tracing/instrumentation and sampling - [x] Rollback policy and smoke tests - [x] Docs + release notes Perf summary (internal perf harness against llama-13b-like workload): - p50 end-to-end latency: -2% (neutral) - p95: -18% - p99: -27% - GPU kernel queue jitter (stddev): -33% - Token-level KV duplications (measured via synthetic overlap load): -42% Notes on tradeoffs and mitigation: - Small accuracy regressions can occur when lossy aggregation merges disjoint token prefixes; to mitigate we only enable it when sample-eval pass rate >= 99.5% on a held-out eval set. - The demux introduces a small classification overhead (~40ns median); overall improvement outweighs cost for interactive SLOs. Related work: builds on prior prefill/decode handoff PRs but takes a routing-first approach rather than kernel-level preemption. Releases: opt-in feature flag: runtime.experimental.prefill_demux default off for 2 weeks, then gradual rollout. Follow-ups: - automatic threshold tuning via Optimize; - extend demux signals with model-architecture-aware features; - add a bounded shared warm cache lane for multi-tenant affinity. Links: Linear ENG-4567 (design doc), benchmark harness in perf/benchmarks/prefill_demux_bench.py, tracing guide: observability/tracing/prefill_provenance_events.md

review_comments: Priya Nair: Could you add a failsafe counter for the coalescer so it doesn't starve fringe ranges? Requesting a test for the counter behavior.
Maya Chen (author): Added a coalescer eviction counter and unit test (see aggregator.cc). It enforces a max-merge-per-shard per-second and is covered in tests.
Diego Alvarez: Nice metrics — can you add a dashboard query example for attributing p99 to demux lanes?
Maya Chen: Added observability queries and a minimal dashboard JSON in perf/benchmarks dir for review.
Connor Blake: I saw slight regressions in a long-sequence gen e2e test when aggregation fidelity > 0.6. Can we gate default to 0.5?
Maya Chen: Default fidelity set to 0.45 and a runtime flag to adjust in prod. Added note to release notes.
merge_details: Merged via squash on 2026-02-22 by Maya Chen. Merge commit summarizes demux, aggregator, smoother, tracing, rollback policy. Feature gated behind runtime.experimental.prefill_demux.
release_notes: Introduces a prefill-decode demultiplexer that reduces tail latency and KV duplication by routing requests into specialized pipeline lanes and applying lossy prefill aggregation with stage smoothing. Opt-in feature flag: runtime.experimental.prefill_demux. Expect p95 improvements for interactive workloads; enable behind flag and monitor pref-fill provenance metrics.
notes_for_ops: Default off. If enabled: monitor tracing tag prefill.demux_lane, coalescer.merge_rate, stage_smoother.queue_jitter and rollback.rate. Rollback recommended if sample-eval pass rate drops below 99.5%.
qa_instructions: Run tests/prefill_demux_unit.cc and perf/benchmarks/prefill_demux_bench.py against a 13B model profile. Validate: (1) p95 < baseline by ~15% on interactive traces, (2) coalescer.merge_rate does not exceed configured max, (3) rollback triggers when sample evals fail.
ops_impact: Minor runtime CPU overhead (~0.02 vCPU per GPU host) from classification and tracing sampling. Significant win in reduced kernel scheduling jitter and less KV eviction churn.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Enable feature flag for 10% of traffic and monitor metrics, 2) Run extended regression suite for long-generation sequences, 3) Add auto-tuning hook in Optimize roadmap
security_considerations: No new surface for secrets. Tracing adds telemetry; sampling defaults to 0.5% and can be tuned. No PII included in provenance tags.
test_plan: Unit tests for classifier thresholds and aggregator eviction counter; perf bench; smoke e2e tests with fallback enabled. All tests included in CI pipeline for this PR.
notes: This PR takes a routing-first approach to the prefill/decode problem; follow-ups will explore kernel-level preemption combined with lane-aware kernel affinity.
